reference.methodBody: As of {asOf}. Latest cached filings only; one issuer per CIK (share classes deduplicated); SEC SIC first 3 digits, same annual or quarterly grain, exact accounting concept and currency. Period ends within 45 days, durations within 15 days. Later filings, missing comparisons and zero or loss bases are excluded. Equal-weight median of company YoY rates — not aggregate industry growth, a full industry census, or a matched business peer set.

financials.conceptBody: YoY = current ÷ prior-year value − 1, against the same period a year earlier rather than the previous quarter. Percentage-point gap = company growth − sample median growth.
financials.yoyNote: Growth is withheld where the prior base was zero or a loss, because a percentage there is not meaningful.

overview.metaDescription: A working system that looked twice as good as it was, why, and what was left after the measurement was fixed.
overview.title: A system that looked twice as good as it was.
overview.lede: This project ranks newly filed SEC disclosures by how likely each is to matter. The interesting part is not the ranking. It is that an early version scored roughly twice as well as the honest one, the reason was a single assumption about a timestamp, and the difference was measured and published rather than quietly fixed.

nav.label: On this page
nav.does: What it does and does not do

problem.title: Too much is filed to read
problem.body1: Public companies file continuously, and most of what they file changes nothing. A person who wants to keep up has to decide, every morning, which of the day's filings are worth opening — and that decision is usually made by headline, by company size, or not at all.
problem.body2: So the question this project asks is narrow and checkable: given everything filed today, which five should be read first? A ranking can be scored against what actually happened afterwards, which is why it was chosen over anything that would require predicting a price.
problem.scale: The evaluation covers {filings} filings over {sessions} sessions, a median of {median} filings per session.

sources.title: Three sources, each with a time of observation

filings.title: SEC filings
filings.body: 8-K disclosures from EDGAR, with the acceptance timestamp kept — the moment the filing became public, not the date printed on it.

prices.title: Daily prices
prices.body: Adjusted daily open, high, low and close, used to measure what happened after a filing and to build the historical pictures on company pages.

fundamentals.title: Company Facts
fundamentals.body: Filed financial figures with their accounting concept, unit and reporting period, used for the filed-results section rather than for the ranking model.

sources.note: Nothing is bought, scraped from a terminal, or hand-entered. Every input is a public filing or a vendor-adjusted price series, and the evaluation records the row count and content hash of each.

does.rank: Ranks the day's filings by the estimated chance of an unusually large benchmark-adjusted move afterwards.
does.measure: Measures that ranking against what happened, on sessions the model never trained on.
does.publish: Publishes the measurement, the failures and the evidence files behind both.

not.advice: It does not give investment advice, price targets or buy and sell calls.
not.direction: It estimates the size of a reaction, never its direction. A large move can go either way.
not.returns: A historical ranking result is not a trading return. Nothing here accounts for costs, slippage, capacity or the price of being wrong.

results.title: What it scored, honestly measured
results.model: Of the five the model ranked first each day, the average share that mattered
results.random: The same measure, picking five at random
results.definition: It is the average share of each day's top five that turned out to be material. It is not the chance of finding at least one material filing in the top five, and it is not a success rate per day. On a typical session with five picks, it means roughly one of them mattered.
results.interval: The 95% interval on average precision runs {low} to {high}, from a cluster bootstrap over sessions with {draws} draws. A point estimate without that interval would suggest more precision than the sample supports.

leakage.title: One assumption about a timestamp
leakage.body1: A filing is accepted at a particular minute, and a reader can only act after it. The first pipeline entered positions on the filing *date* instead — which, for a filing accepted after the close, means entering before it existed. Nothing else about the model changed.
leakage.body2: Measured on the same sessions, the shortcut scored {naive} where the honest pipeline scores {honest}. Each row below removes one more thing the model should not have known.
leakage.caption: Each stage removes one source of hindsight. The last row is the pipeline that produces every published number.

failures.title: Three things that were tried and not shipped
failures.intro: Written as a list of negatives on purpose. All three were measured with the same machinery as the positive results and reported the same way.

text.title: Language features from the filing text
text.body: Sentiment and change-detection features over the filing body did not improve the ranking beyond what arrival time and item code already carried.

selfRelative.title: Issuer-relative scoring as a ranking signal
selfRelative.body: Comparing a filing with its own issuer's history is useful on a company page, and it did not improve the cross-sectional daily ranking.

volatility.title: Volatility forecasting
volatility.body: A forecaster only appears on a company page when it passes its out-of-sample coverage gate. When none does, the card is absent rather than approximate.

product.title: What is running
product.intro: The research engine refreshes filings, prices and filed results on a schedule and regenerates every company page from them. The site you are reading is the output, and each number on it links to the filing or price series behind it.

noEvidence.title: The evidence package is not in this build
noEvidence.body: This page states numbers only from the exported evidence files. They are not present here, so nothing is shown rather than a figure typed in by hand.

research.metaDescription: The research question, the point-in-time rules, the leakage audit, the ranking metrics with intervals, the baselines, the ablations and the limitations.
research.title: How this is measured, and what the measurement cannot say.
research.lede: Every figure on this page is read from the exported evidence package at build time. None of them is written into the page, so none can drift from the run that produced it.

question.title: The research question
question.body1: Given the set of 8-K filings accepted before a session's entry point, can they be ranked so that the ones followed by an unusually large benchmark-adjusted move appear near the top?
question.body2: This is a ranking question, scored per session, not a return question. It asks which filings deserve attention first, and it is answerable with public data and checkable against what happened.

method.title: Labels, windows and validation
method.label: Label
method.labelValue: A benchmark-adjusted move of at least {threshold} standard deviations in the event window.
method.windowValue: {sessions} sessions from the first eligible entry.
method.estimationValue: {sessions} sessions of market-model estimation, ending {gap} sessions before the event.

pit.title: What the model is allowed to know
pit.entry: Entry happens at the first session that opens after the filing's acceptance timestamp. A filing accepted after the close is entered the next session, never the same one.
pit.features: Trailing features end the session before entry. A trailing volatility window that includes the event day is a window that contains the answer.
pit.universe: The universe at each date is the universe as it was known then, not the set of issuers that still exist today.
pit.history: Issuer history is restricted to filings whose outcomes had already resolved at the decision point.

leakage.title: The leakage ladder
leakage.intro: Each row removes one source of hindsight and re-runs the whole evaluation. The first row is a pipeline that looks strong and is not; the last is the one that produces every published number.
leakage.caption: Each stage removes one source of hindsight, measured end to end.

metrics.title: Ranking metrics
metrics.caption: Headline metrics from the honest pipeline.
metrics.dailyPrecisionMeaning: The average share of each session's top five that turned out to be material.
metrics.randomPrecisionMeaning: The same measure with five filings drawn at random from the same session.
metrics.averagePrecisionMeaning: Area under the precision-recall curve over all filings, not per session.
metrics.rocAucMeaning: The chance a random material filing is ranked above a random immaterial one.
metrics.baseRateMeaning: The share of all evaluated filings that were followed by a material move.
metrics.definitionLabel: Precision@5 is an average share, not a hit rate.
metrics.definition: It is the average share of each day's top five that turned out to be material — not the probability of finding at least one material filing among them, and not a per-day success rate.
metrics.uncertainty: Intervals come from a {method} with {draws} draws over {sessions} sessions. Average precision: {apLow} to {apHigh} at 95%.

baselines.title: Compared with rules that need no model
baselines.intro: A model is only interesting against the cheap rules it is meant to beat. All of these are scored on the same sessions, the same way.
baselines.caption: Daily top-five share for each selection rule.

ablations.title: What each group of features adds
ablations.intro: Each row removes one group and re-scores. A group that changes nothing is reported as changing nothing.
ablations.caption: Feature-group ablations, re-scored end to end.
ablations.missingTitle: Ablation table not in this build
ablations.missingBody: The ablation export is not present in the evidence package staged for this build, so no table is shown.

limitations.title: What this cannot tell you
limitations.universe: The universe is a convenience sample of currently listed large caps. It is not survivorship-controlled, so it cannot speak to issuers that delisted.
limitations.costs: No transaction cost, spread, slippage or capacity assumption is applied anywhere. A ranking result is not a strategy result.
limitations.magnitude: The label is the magnitude of a move, not its direction. Nothing here says which way a price went or will go.
limitations.coverage: Dynamic events are published for AAPL, JPM and NVDA only. Other companies still have filings, filed results and price history.
limitations.generalisation: Results are measured on US 8-K disclosures over the evaluated sessions and should not be assumed to carry to other filing types, markets or periods.

precision.definition: Of the k items ranked highest, the share that turned out to be material. Averaged over sessions when it is called daily precision@k.

averagePrecision.definition: The area under the precision-recall curve: one number summarising how well the ranking separates material from immaterial across every threshold.

rocAuc.definition: The probability that a randomly chosen material filing is ranked above a randomly chosen immaterial one. 0.5 is chance.

baseRate.definition: How often the thing being predicted happens at all. Every precision figure has to be read against it.

walkForward.definition: Train on the past, test on the future, repeatedly moving forward in time — rather than shuffling all dates together.

purged.definition: Dropping training examples whose outcome windows overlap the test period, so an answer cannot reach the model through an overlapping window.

pointInTime.definition: Using only what was knowable at the decision moment: the universe as it was, the prices as they had printed, and the filings already accepted.

noEvidence.body: This page reports numbers only from the exported evidence files, and they are not present here. Run the evidence export and rebuild.

earnings.metaDescription: The estimated earnings calendar was retired. Filed results now live on each company page, with the filing they came from.
earnings.title: Financial results moved to the company pages.
earnings.body: The estimated reporting calendar has been withdrawn. Each company page now shows the latest filed report instead: the figures as filed, the reporting period they cover, the year-ago comparison and a link to the filing itself.
earnings.why: It was withdrawn because the dates on it were inferred from each issuer's past reporting cadence rather than confirmed by the company, and an inferred date on a calendar reads as a confirmed one.
earnings.boundary: No future reporting date is published anywhere on this site unless the company or a filing has confirmed it.
